Guidance & outlook: Slippage ratio is contained at 0.60% and which is improved by 20 basis points YoY. - So whatever the performance we have given, we have bettered everywhere on count of guidance whatever we have given.
See business growth, we gave guidance of 10-11% which is now at 14.37%.
CASA we said that it will be between 30-32% but that guidance was for March 27, we have 29.70% as of now.
Growth & demand: Then global advances grew at a handsome rate of 17.97% YoY at 12.93381 lakhs crores.
15.12% YoY growth we have registered under MSME and it is at 1,68,815 crores.
2.19% growth we have given YoY basis on earning per share that is placed at 21.47%.
Margins & costs: YoY credit cost has also reduced by 23 basis points and now it is at 0.49% only.
Trade cost we envisaged at 0.75% but which is improved at 0.51% only.
So we have come up with very nice products also. - So our endeavor is to slowly and steadily replace those high cost bulk deposit through not necessarily 100% by CASA but through retail deposits.
Capex & expansion: So, we are getting agency commission also and at the same time valuation of these companies with the good business is growing.
And is it fair to say that margin expansion from here that you are indicating will be driven more by reduction in deposit cost versus lending yields? - Mr.
But that is on account of two, there are some incomes which are booked in the last quarter like many commission on government, many service charges.
Balance sheet & cash: I know there are many benefits of growing RAM, considering the better leverage also there, diversified risk also, less credit cost also and at times priority sector reckoning also.
And that is a growing business and it gives us good leverage.
And, again, in MSME, a little more leverage is there.
Risks & challenges: That time, yields were softened so we could earn through treasury operations by sale of investments.
And soft target we have kept at threshold at 1.10, 110%.
But we will see how things evolve. - Interviewer: - Sir, the reason I ask is then, you know, the 1% ROA comes under some sort of pressure if we start seeing higher credit cost.

Guidance & outlook: International Monetary Fund (IMF) latest growth projections (April 2026 World Economic Outlook) show a resilient but fragile global economy, as global GDP growth has been estimated at approximately 3.4% in 2025, before moderating to 3.1% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027 under the assumption of a contained geopolitical conflict.
GDP growth rate for the last quarter of FY26 is expected to be closer to 7.5% buoyed by consumption and public investment.
Despite multiple headwinds, major international agencies forecast Indian economy to grow around 6.5% in FY27.
Growth & demand: Considering these domestic and global macroeconomic factors, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has projected real GDP growth at 6.9% for FY 2027.
Favourable domestic macroeconomic conditions have fuelled credit growth of 15% for FY26.

BUSINESS PERFORMANCE During FY 2025-26, the global business of the Bank stood at `28,06,226 Crores with a growth of 12.11% y-o-y from `25,03,194 Crores, with global deposits at `15,68,678 Crores with a growth of 9.71% y-o-y and global advances at `12,37,548 Crores with a growth rate of 15.30%.
Margins & costs: Tight liquidity conditions in the Banking system for the most part of FY25 also constrained margins of banks as they had to endure higher cost of funds.
PROFITABILITY The Bank has growth of 12.69% y-o-y in net profit to `19,187 Crores in FY 2025-26 with operating profit growing by 5.19% y-o-y to `33,019 Crores.
Net Interest Margin (NIM) of the Bank decline by 22 bps at 2.51% in March 2026 from 2.73% in March 2025.
Capex & expansion: As per available estimates from the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) and multilateral institutions, India's real GDP growth for FY 2025-26 is estimated in the range of 7.4%-7.6%, supported by broad-based expansion across services, manufacturing and investment activity.
The growth was driven by strong credit expansion, with Global Advances increasing by 15.30% to `12,37,548 Crores, while Global Deposits grew by 9.71% to `15,68,678 Crores.

Apart from trading profit, other major sources of non-interest income, like, service charges (`3,914 Crores), commission and exchange (`1,792 Crores), recovery from written off accounts (`6,537 Crores) and Profit from exchange transaction (`1,471 Crores) contributed to the non-interest income of the Bank.
Balance sheet & cash: TAX DEDUCTED AT SOURCE (TDS) ON DIVIDEND PAYMENT a) Pursuant to Provision of Income Tax Act, 1961, as amended by the Finance Act, 2020, dividend income is taxable in the hands of Shareholders w.e.f.

Dividend The Board of Directors of the Bank has recommended a dividend of `4.20 per equity share (i.e., 210%) of face value of `2/- each to the Shareholders for the year 2025-26, subject to the approval of the Shareholders at the AGM.
The Board recommended a dividend of 210% (` 4.20 per equity share of face value `2 each) for the financial year.
Risks & challenges: Inflationary pressures, which had eased through much of 2025, witnessed renewed upside risks due to higher energy prices and supply-side disruptions.
Despite the challenges, I am delighted to announce that our global business surpassed `28 Lakh Crores with a robust 12.11% y-o-y growth in Net Profit to `19,187 Crores (12 Months).
The Gross NPA ratio declined by 110 bps y-o-y to 1.84% this year and Net NPA declined by 27 bps y-o-y to 0.43%.
